trigger_or_context: You are getting to know someone new. You feel a pull to stay closed off so you don't get used again.
short_term_function: Staying guarded keeps you feeling safe. You don't have to risk getting used or hurt again.
developmental_cost: When your guard is always up, people never get a chance to show you who they really are. So you can't tell safe people from unsafe ones.
adaptive_alternative_1: Notice when your guard is up. Let it down a little in small, safe ways. Then watch how the person treats you before you open more.
what_new_response_supports: You get to see if this person is really safe, instead of guessing. You learn who has earned more of your trust.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Letting your guard down even a little can feel scary. You may feel unsure for a while.
context_conditions: If someone has shown they hurt you, or your safety is at risk, keeping your guard up is smart. This is only about people who have not shown they are unsafe.
review_reason: Context-dependent: guardedness can be healthy pacing or a wall that blocks real information. The meaning depends on whether it is calibrated to what the person actually shows, so the alternative stays conditional.
